title: A practice for today
lede: Each day of the week has its planet, its question and its mantras. Begin with a few quiet minutes, guided step by step, or open the day’s mantras and chant one. Everything you do here stays on this device: nothing is sent anywhere.

rite.title: Six quiet steps
rite.lede: Choose how long you have. The day’s opening prayer, a main mantra of your choosing, and a closing prayer. Each step waits for you; skip any you like.

steps.name: Arrive
steps.title: Arrive
steps.text: Sit comfortably. Follow the circle: in as it grows, out as it settles. Breathe gently and never strain.

steps.name: Light
steps.title: Light the lamp
steps.text: Light a real diya if you have one, or this one. Let its flame be the centre of your attention for a moment.

steps.name: Open
steps.title: The opening prayer
steps.text: Begin with the day’s opening prayer. Read it once, slowly, aloud or silently; the meaning is beneath it.

steps.name: Intend
steps.title: Set an intention
steps.text: Sit with the day’s question for a moment. Then name what you bring today: a word is enough. You may also bring nothing at all.

steps.name: Chant
steps.title: The main mantra
steps.text: Choose one of today’s mantras, or one of your own. Repeat it as many times as feels true: tap the circle, the button, or press space. One careful recitation is enough.

steps.name: Close
steps.title: Close
steps.text: Close with a prayer for everyone. If something is ready to be set down, write it and offer it to the fire.

rite.keepJournal: Keep this in my practice journal (on this device only)
rite.mantraNote: Om Krīm Kālikāyai Namaḥ · the mantra is chosen with Sarvakali
rite.offerLabel: What would you like to let go of?
rite.closing: Sit for a breath longer. What you set down today can stay down. Return to your day gently.
rite.doneText: Thank you for coming. Come back tomorrow, at the same time if you can: a little each day is the practice.
rite.reflection: A line for your journal (optional, kept on this device)
rite.question: A question for the day

log.title: Day by day
log.lede: Kept only in this browser, never sent. A filled day means you practised.
log.empty: Nothing yet. Your days and journal will appear here as you practise.
log.clearConfirm: Clear your practice record and journal from this device? This cannot be undone.

month.title: A month of lunar days
month.lede: Each day’s tithi, worked out from the moon at sunrise in India, with the sacred days marked. Close to a panchang, but it can differ by a day near a change; Sarvakali’s panchang decides.

days.title: The nights that matter
days.lede: New and full moons are worked out from the moon itself (to within a few hours; a panchang gives the exact tithi). Festival dates are from public calendars, to be confirmed with Sarvakali’s panchang.
days.amavasyaNote: The new moon, a night especially kept for Kali.
days.amavasyaDo: A suggestion: light a lamp after dark, sit in silence for a few minutes, and offer what you are ready to release.
days.purnimaDo: A suggestion: a slow evening, gratitude for what has grown, and the mala once round.

reminder.title: A gentle daily reminder
reminder.text: Add a reminder to your own calendar, every day at the time you choose. It works today, with no sign-up.
reminder.add: Add a daily reminder to my calendar
reminder.addedNote: Saved. Open the file to add a daily reminder to your calendar.

week.title: A week of planetary days
week.lede: The library follows the seven planetary weekdays, as the Western and Indian weekday systems share them. The planets are symbolism for reflection, not a forecast: any mantra may be practised on any day.

todayList.title: For today
todayList.lede: The day’s own mantras, prayers and verses. Open one to read it slowly, hear how it sounds, and chant it.
todayList.all: All of {day}’s mantras, with their meanings

mine.title: The ones you keep
mine.lede: Tap ✦ on any mantra to keep it here, with how often you have chanted it. Kept on this device only.
mine.empty: None yet. Tap ✦ on any mantra in the library to keep it here.

library.title: Mantras, prayers and verses for every day
library.lede: Each with its Sanskrit, a transliteration, a readable pronunciation, its meaning in simple English, and when and how it can be used. Search by day, deity or intention.
